Classify a pedon under the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001)

Source: R/key-cst.R
classify_cst2001.Rd

Keys a PedonRecord through the Chinese Soil Taxonomy (Cooperative Research Group on Chinese Soil Taxonomy, 2001, the English edition published by Science Press). Experimental: this release keys the 14 orders (key 5.1: Histosols, Anthrosols, Spodosols, Andosols, Ferralosols, Vertosols, Aridosols, Halosols, Gleyosols, Isohumosols, Ferrosols, Argosols, Cambosols and Primosols), their 39 suborders and their 138 groups (key 5.2), with soilKey's residuals [E2] [Other Ferralosols], [A1.4] [Other Permagelic Histosols] and [A2.5] [Other Orthic Histosols] where the book prints none (the name stops there, with a note). Since v0.9.375 it keys the subgroups of orders A to G (176, with [A1.3.x] Lithic Hemi-Permagelic Histosols, listed in Appendix 1 only, at its Appendix position); their criteria are written as presets (inst/rules/cst2001/presets.yaml), expanded when the rules are loaded. The groups of orders H to N stop at the group, with a note, until their subgroups follow in a later release.

Usage

classify_cst2001(
  pedon,
  rules = NULL,
  on_missing = c("warn", "silent", "error"),
  gapfill = FALSE
)

Arguments

pedon

A PedonRecord.

rules

Optional pre-loaded rule set (load_rules("cst2001")).

on_missing

One of "warn" (default), "silent", "error".

gapfill

Opt-in within-pedon gap-fill, as in classify_usda.

Value

A ClassificationResult with system_id "cst2001", the subgroup (or the deepest class assigned) in name, the order in rsg_or_order, the classes of each level in levels (with name_pt and book_provisional), the key trace with the horizon panel, provisional_because, and, when a class was assigned on a provisional reading, in candidates the class the key would reach without it (kind "alternative").

Details

The key is read in the book's order, the first class whose criteria pass assigned, as the book prescribes (each class lacks the properties of the classes before it). The criteria read the 33 diagnostic horizons and the 25 diagnostic characteristics of chapter 3 on the recorded data (see identify_horizons with "cst2001"), with their weaker evidence grades where the book gives them, the soil moisture and temperature regimes (recorded on the site, or from the aridity index, the site's records of paddy, groundwater and permafrost, and the air temperature), and the few criteria the key defines where it uses them. Every test is three-valued: a measurement not recorded leaves it undecided, a field observation not recorded is absent. A class tested before the assigned one that could not be decided makes the name provisional (provisional_because); a class assigned on a reading the book leaves open (gley colours without a ferrous-iron test, cracks observed for their duration) carries a warning; a class the book itself marks provisional is noted as such (levels$book_provisional).

Names are the English of the book, in the plural of the key ("Permagelic Histosols"), with soilKey's Portuguese gloss in levels$name_pt. The approximate equivalents of the order in US Soil Taxonomy (1999) and the WRB (1998), Tables 4.2 and 4.3, are added as a note (qualifiers$correlation_cst and a line in warnings); they never change the classification. A residual suborder or group named for the udic regime (the Udic Andosols, Vertosols, Isohumosols, Ferrosols, Argosols and Cambosols, the Udi- groups) or for the aquic one (the Aqui-Orthic Halosols) reached by a soil whose regime read is another keeps its class, with a note. The diagnostic horizons and characteristics of each layer are in the trace (phase horizons). The readings where the text is silent are listed in system.file("rules", "cst2001", "readings.yaml", package = "soilKey").

References

Cooperative Research Group on Chinese Soil Taxonomy (2001). Chinese Soil Taxonomy. Science Press, Beijing and New York.

See also

make_cst2001_example, identify_horizons, soilkey_systems.

Examples

res <- classify_cst2001(make_cst2001_example("K3"), on_missing = "silent")
res$name
#> [1] "Typic Argi-Udic Ferrosols"
res$levels
#>       level   code                      name
#> 1    orders      K                 Ferrosols
#> 2 suborders     K3            Udic Ferrosols
#> 3    groups   K3.4       Argi-Udic Ferrosols
#> 4 subgroups K3.4.7 Typic Argi-Udic Ferrosols
#>                                name_pt book_provisional
#> 1              Ferrossolos (Ferrosols)            FALSE
#> 2                   Ferrossolos údicos            FALSE
#> 3         Ferrossolos údicos argílicos            FALSE
#> 4 Ferrossolos údicos argílicos típicos            FALSE
